summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge: analyze Soony's launch data, then build a general recheck-and-act agent product (poller, extraction, recompute, supplier emails, approvals, phone alerts) with a demo and pitch ready by the 12:00 Sunday hand-in.
summary.outcome: Found that Soony's plan hid real shortfalls (overbooked art books, failed statues, card shortages) and built a working product with a Today/Launch UI, versioned polling, approval flow, phone-call bridge and a flexible CSV column mapper. Demo script, rehearsal of three stories and live/demo instances are done; the video, deck and several polish items remain.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhooks. Changes must be detected by polling and comparing SHA-256, since files are replaced under the same name.
Confidential portal data lives in gitignored data/; .env is gitignored and .env.example is committed.

Live and demo instances run side by side and share one alert database; demo is started via scripts/demo.sh (reset, restart, stop), with CALLS=twilio|openai enabling real calls and ASK_PUBLIC_URL needed for keypad answers.
Calls are dry_run by default; ASK_CARD_ALERTS=off disables the case-to-phone bridge on live. The OpenAI realtime webhook is configured in the OpenAI project settings and points to a single instance.
Web UI polls state every 5s (POLL_MS) and routine data every 15s; no server push.

Export CSVs arrive with varying encodings, delimiters, German/SAP column names and ragged rows, so columns.py maps synonyms to canonical fields, with a cached gpt-4.1-mini fallback for unknown headers.
Team workflow uses CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md; work is on branch jonas/today-flow; Entire checkpoints only when repo files change.

code.finding: New synonym-based column mapper (English, German, SAP) that recognises files by their canonical columns and handles decimal commas, German dates and line numbers in tens.
Bridge between today's cases and phone alerts: raises one alert for red or soon-due untouched cases, applies phone decisions to cases exactly once, and closes alerts if the case is decided elsewhere.

Realtime call path (Twilio to SIP to OpenAI Realtime); switched to semantic VAD with low eagerness, no overlapping responses, and reconnect up to twice after the first test call suffered from noise-triggered interruptions.

workflow: Subagents are effective for large cross-checks (200 order confirmations plus 59 scans) and for isolated builds like the phone bridge and column mapping.
Verify UI behavior in a headless browser (e.g. pressing J ten times and counting highlighted rows) rather than trusting the code reading.
Ask before actions that cost money (Twilio about $0.38 per minute, OpenAI Realtime) or send real external emails; keep demo and live separated.
Reset the demo instance before every rehearsal and before the pitch.

friction: Cloudflare Tunnel error 1033 on the demo host came from DNS briefly pointing at the wrong tunnel.
Demo server's background loop did not raise phone alerts automatically; the call had to be triggered by hand and the cause is not yet found.
First realtime call failed: background noise was heard as speech, causing 'active response' errors and a dropped connection after about 20 seconds.
OpenAI webhook points at one instance, so a realtime call from the demo required editing it in the OpenAI dashboard.
A demo.sh edit silently did not apply because the line looked different than expected, so a restart did not happen.
New CSV drops had unexpected encodings and rows with extra fields, breaking the paper check and verifier readers until they were made robust.
Safari caches favicons stubbornly, so the old icon may still show.
J/K navigation and highlight were inconsistent with folded groups until changed to row-by-row.
open_items: Deliver the 3-minute video and the 6-slide deck by the 12:00 hand-in.
Fix why the demo server does not raise phone alerts automatically.
Re-test the realtime voice call (about $1) with the new semantic VAD, then switch calls off on the demo (scripts/demo.sh restart without CALLS).
Decide whether to restore the OpenAI webhook to the live address after the demo.
Optional polish: replay supplier replies on the demo, fold the count questions into one case, 'what still saves it' on Launch, a top bar for Maren.
Push the unpushed commits on jonas/today-flow.
Show the 'mapped' data-health notes on the Launch page (needs a frontend change); the contract redline PDF is unopened.
Register sender email addresses in the portal Settings and decide on the Karton Nowak offer; clarify with Lio whether portal data differs per team.
Delete or keep the older Claude doc after the briefing page was published; consider changing the portal password that was posted in Discord.
